findings.problem: Four proofs redo the same argument: for angles 0 ≤ a < b ≤ π, `(exp(a·I) − exp(b·I)).re = cos a − cos b > 0`. The proofs are `unitArc_g_slitPlane_before`, `unitArc_neg_g_slitPlane_after`, and both halves of `unitArc_log_final`. Each one rewrites with `exp_real_angle_I`, unfolds the real part, proves the angle ordering and range bounds with `nlinarith`, and then calls `Real.cos_lt_cos_of_nonneg_of_le_pi`. The two slitPlane lemmas also repeat a complex-subtraction `show … from by push_cast; ring` and a final `nlinarith`. `unitArc_log_final` only restates the same facts at t = t₀ ∓ δ, which the slitPlane lemmas already give.
findings.proposed_change: Add one private lemma, e.g. `unitArc_re_exp_sub_pos {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hab : a < b) (hb : b ≤ Real.pi) : 0 < (exp (↑a * I) - exp (↑b * I)).re`. Proof sketch: `simp only [Complex.sub_re, Complex.exp_ofReal_mul_I_re]` (or `exp_real_angle_I` then `simp`), then `linarith [Real.cos_lt_cos_of_nonneg_of_le_pi ha hb hab]`. The `before` lemma becomes `rw [mem_slitPlane_iff]; left; rw [h_s_arc]; exact unitArc_re_exp_sub_pos h0 hθ_lt hπ`. The `after` lemma does the same after `neg_sub`, with a = θ₀' and b = θ. `unitArc_log_final` is then the two applications at t₀−δ and t₀+δ, or it follows from the slit lemmas with `mem_slitPlane_iff`. Only the angle range facts, `0 ≤ θ` and `θ ≤ π`, remain at each use. The hypotheses (`ht₀_Ioo`, `htt₀`, `ht3`, `ht1`) are unchanged.
findings.benefit: The cos-monotonicity real-part argument is stated and proved once. The three roughly 20-line proofs shrink to range checks plus one `exact`. The proofs no longer rely on the fragile `simp only` real-part normal forms, which differ between the copies. A future change to the arc parametrization then needs one edit.

findings.problem: Five times the proof converts a segment result `piece_i : IntervalIntegrable (deriv h/h) ∧ ∫ = v` into the same statement for `deriv g/g`. Each conversion calls `unitArc_logDeriv_ae_eq`, then `congr_ae` with `ae_restrict_iff' measurableSet_uIoc` and `.mono`, and then `integral_congr_ae` with the same `.mono`. Only the interval and the piece change. This gives five `h_ae_*`, five `hint_*` and five `h_ftc_*` blocks, about 45 lines of identical a.e. transfer reasoning. `piece₁` and `piece₂` also repeat the same derivative-continuity side goal (lines 461–472). The measure-theoretic argument is not trivial, and it is hidden in repeated boilerplate.
findings.proposed_change: Extend the existing `unitArc_logDeriv_ae_eq` into a lemma that transfers the whole piece. For example: `private lemma unitArc_piece_transfer {lo hi : ℝ} {v : ℂ} (hle : lo ≤ hi) (g h : ℝ → ℂ) (hg : ∀ t, lo < t → t < hi → g t = h t) (hd : ∀ t ∈ Ioo lo hi, deriv g t = deriv h t) (hp : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => deriv h t / h t) volume lo hi ∧ ∫ t in lo..hi, deriv h t / h t = v) : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => deriv g t / g t) volume lo hi ∧ ∫ t in lo..hi, deriv g t / g t = v`. Proof: take `h_ae := unitArc_logDeriv_ae_eq hle g h hg hd`. The integrability half is `hp.1.congr_ae` applied to `(ae_restrict_iff' measurableSet_uIoc).mpr (h_ae.mono …)`. The integral half is `(intervalIntegral.integral_congr_ae (h_ae.mono …)).trans hp.2`. In `unitArc_ftc_value` each segment becomes `obtain ⟨hint_34, h_ftc_34⟩ := unitArc_piece_transfer (by norm_num) g h₃ (fun t h3 h4 => hg_h₃ t h3 h4.le) hderiv_3 piece₃`. The other four segments follow the same pattern with their existing `hg_*` and `hderiv_*` hypotheses. The `hint_*` and `h_ftc_*` names used later stay the same, so the splitting and telescoping part is unchanged. The continuity side goals for the arc pieces can likewise share one `have hcont_deriv_arc` for piece₁ and piece₂.
findings.benefit: The 45-line block shrinks to five short calls. The a.e. argument is written once and checked once. Adding or changing a boundary segment then means editing one line per segment instead of three coordinated blocks.
